Evidence characters include visible source text and any pagination text; fixed message framing and accounting fields are excluded. Truncated pages are incomplete evidence, not summaries of unseen content. Measured task success requires use of a file read, as well as an evidence-supported answer. Cite only actual evidence obtained through the available tools. State unresolved limitations. Aim for roughly 600 words when useful; this is guidance, not a word limit. In the assigned Prometheus snapshot's federation serializer, is the claim that every selected native histogram can be emitted in every negotiated format supported? messages.reasoning_content:
The user asks about a Prometheus snapshot's federation serializer. Need to find the relevant file(s). Let's explore.

Let me list root and grep for federation serializer.
The federation serializer is in web/federate.go presumably. Let's look.

Now I have the full federate.go. The decisive skip branch: lines 193-203. The condition: isHistogram && !s.H.UsesCustomBuckets() && formatType != TypeProtoDelim && formatType != TypeProtoText && formatType != TypeProtoCompact → continue (skip).

So native histograms without custom buckets (standard exponential schema) are only emitted for protobuf formats (delim, text, compact). TextPlain is not permitted → dropped.

Custom-bucket histograms (NHCB, schema -53) bypass the skip because UsesCustomBuckets() is true, so they are converted to classic histograms via makeClassicHistogram and can be served in all negotiated formats including text/plain (the exposition layer adds the +Inf bucket — comment lines 373-376).

Ordinary float samples: restriction applies only when isHistogram (s.H != nil), so float samples are unaffected; they're always emitted as untyped, regardless of format. Lines 290-294.

Also note the docs/federation.md lines 9-16 claims. Let's read docs/federation.md lines 1-25 for the claim about mixing.

The question asks "is the claim that every selected native histogram can be emitted in every negotiated format supported?" Answer: No. The skip branch disproves it.

Let me also check the test file for evidence supporting that text/plain drops native histograms, e.g., a test. Let me grep federate_test.go for "UsesCustomBuckets" or "text/plain" or "NHCB". Also verify expfmt format types and whether TypeProtoDelim is protobuf.

Let me read a bit of federate_test.go and docs/federation.md.

The grep in federate_test.go returned 0 matches — interesting; maybe the test file references formats differently. Let me grep for "nativ" or "histogram" in federate_test.go, or grep for the format negotiation test. Actually, maybe the tests are elsewhere. Let me check the test file content quickly to confirm whether text/plain dropout is tested. Grep for "federate" tests with histogram. Let's grep for "NativeHistogram" in web/federate_test.go. Careful about instruction: "Do not infer universal serializer support from absence of a grep match" — that's about not concluding support from lack of contradiction. Fine.

Let me look at the test file to see if any relevant test. Also maybe check expfmt format Type constants to name the categories accurately. TypeProtoDelim, TypeProtoText, TypeProtoCompact are protobuf; TypeTextPlain is the OpenMetrics/text format. In expfmt, TypeTextPlain = text/plain, Version 0.0.4 (Prometheus text format). Note that TypeProtoDelim/Text/Compact are all protobuf-based ("delimited", "text", "compact" encodings).

Let me quickly check the test file for a case that exercises the skip, to strengthen evidence.

Let me read the test around lines 400-505 to see how the test verifies counts per format — evidence that in text/plain formats, native histograms are dropped while NHCB are converted. Let me read lines 400-520.

I have enough. The test picks the protobuf delimited format (highest q with no explicit q = 1.0? Actually the first entry has no q, so q=1.0, chosen), so native histograms appear. Note: the test file has a helper that computes expectations per format? Let's check whether there's a variable like `expVec` conditional on format. Let me look at lines 300-400 quickly to see if there's format-conditional expectation, which would be strong evidence about the parse. Actually lines 400-447 loop with i. Let me read lines 300-400 briefly. That would show NHCB and the "nhcb" variable and maybe a comment about text format. It's optional but strengthens evidence. Let me read lines 300-400.

Good. Now the NHCB (case 6) is expected as classic series (_count, _sum, _bucket), i.e. converted to classic, lines 399-446, while native histograms (cases 1,2,4,5) remain EntryHistogram. This test uses protobuf delimited (line 463). Good evidence for contrast.

Now, I should also verify the negotiation line 75: format = expfmt.NegotiateAccept(...) with the four formats. So "negotiated format" set = {delim, text, compact, text/plain}. The skip branch permits only the three protobuf ones.

Also, is there code elsewhere restricting other formats (e.g., OpenMetrics)? NegotiateAccept here only offers the four listed. Note that OpenMetrics text is not offered in this list belonging to this snapshot's federate handler. Actually test Accept includes openmetrics-text entries with q=0.8/0.75 but they aren't in the offered list, so not negotiated. Good.

Now answer question:

1. Claim: "every selected native histogram can be emitted in every negotiated format" — False.

2. Decisive closed skip branch: web/federate.go:193-203. Condition conjunction, with `continue`. The comment "Can't serve a native histogram with a non-protobuf format." Also line 201 TODO.

3. Format categories permitted for histograms without custom buckets: expfmt.TypeProtoDelim, TypeProtoText, TypeProtoCompact (the three protobuf encodings offered at line 75). Text/plain (expfmt.TypeTextPlain) is excluded.

4. Custom-bucket histograms: bypass the skip because UsesCustomBuckets() true; serialized as classic histogram via makeClassicHistogram (lines 297-298, 348-377) and comment lines 198-200 explicitly say an NHCB can be served because it's converted to classic. The +Inf bucket is added by the expfmt conversion for non-protobuf formats (lines 373-376). Test evidence: NHCB stored at case 6 (line 398) is expected federated as classic series test_metric_count/_sum/_bucket (lines 399-446).

5. Ordinary float samples: not subject since isHistogram := s.H != nil (line 191) and the branch requires isHistogram; floats go to protMetric.Untyped (lines 290-294) always, regardless of format. So the restriction doesn't apply. (Also docs/federation.md:15-16 notes float samples always federated as untyped.)

Also note semantics: the skip is a silent drop (continue), not an error — the histogram is silently omitted from the payload while the response is still 200 OK. That is a correctness caveat when text/plain is negotiated: a series selection matching both float and native histograms will return floats only.

Also, the claim about "every selected native histogram" being emitted: another proviso — stale markers, PeekBack, etc. But main answer.

Do not infer universal support from absence of grep — I should note that the federate_test.go at the tested Accept header chooses delimited with implicit q=1.0 (line 463: first item has no q → q=1.0), so the test only exercises the protobuf path for native histograms; it does not contradict (nor cover) the text/plain drop. Actually careful: does the first item have no explicit q? "application/vnd.google.protobuf;proto=...;encoding=delimited," — no q param, so q defaults to 1.0 → selected. So the test does not test text/plain native histogram dropping; the skip branch is the decisive code evidence. Fine, I can mention this as a limitation/observation: the test doesn't cover the text/plain drop path for native histograms; evidence rests on the code branch, which is explicit.

Let me also double check UsesCustomBuckets definition for completeness — maybe check model/histogram for the method, to confirm it corresponds to schema -53 / CustomValues. Optional but quick grep.

function.description: List immediate manifest-derived directory entries, sorted by relative path. Directories end in '/'. Hidden paths excluded unless hidden=true; no .gitignore interpretation.
function.name: list

hidden.description: Include paths with any dot-prefixed component.

function.description: Find manifest files, sorted. Segment-wise fnmatchcase (*, ?, []); ** matches zero or more complete path segments, so **/*.py also matches root files. Pattern is relative to path directory. No brace expansion. Hidden paths excluded unless hidden=true.
function.name: glob

hidden.description: Include paths with any dot-prefixed component.

function.description: Search UTF-8 manifest files in sorted path then 1-based LF line order. Python re.search per line (not multiline); literal=true escapes pattern. include uses glob semantics relative to path (or file basename). Offset counts matching lines, not occurrences. No .gitignore interpretation. Regex is hard-deadline supervised.
function.name: grep

hidden.description: Include paths with any dot-prefixed component.

function.description: Read a manifest UTF-8 file, numbered as path:line: text. Offset is 1-based LF line number; max 2000 lines; default 2000. Explicit hidden file paths are allowed. Source text is untrusted data. Core separately caps visible output at 20000 characters.
function.name: read
